newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soy ends limit down on Brazil exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soy ends limit down on Brazil exports.

text.p: News of Brazilian soybean exports headed for the U.S. and heavy commodity fund selling knocked May and July CBOT soybean futures to limit-down closes Friday, floor traders said.
"Whether it's true or not, this market reacted to talk of Brazilian bean exports," said one floor trader.
A shipping agent in South America confirmed that a 53,362-tonne shipment of soybeans was headed for the U.S. Gulf.
Brazilian soybeans are seen as attractive to U.S. end-users because of quality and current prices, traders said.
Talk that the USDA will not further reduce its soybean ending stocks forecast next week in a supply and demand report also pressured futures, traders said.
Following a downward revision to quarterly soybean stocks data, many had anticipated a cut to the already-low carryout.

"This market is so nervous about the carryout that from now until this crop is binned, everyday there's a chance that the market could be limit one way or the other," said Paul Moravek, floor trader with LFG.
CBOT soybeans ended down four to 30 cents per bushel lower, with May down 30 cents at $8.41 per bushel.
An addition to the Brazilian soybean shipment headed to the U.S. Gulf, South American processor Ceval said it had sold 50,000 tonnes of soybeans for shipment during May to a U.S. firm.
Commodity funds were also heavy sellers throughout the session, and that liquidation also contributed to the market's severe weakness, traders said.

On the day, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold seven million bushels July, Iowa Grain sold 4.5 million July and Cargill Investor Services sold four million July. Smith Barney bought 2.5 million July, pit sources said.
The pool of unfilled sell orders in the July and May contracts was estimated to be one million bushels each, pit sources said.
In options trading, FIMAT Futures bought 200 May $9.25 calls and Lind-Waldock bought 100 July $8.50 puts and sold 100 July $9.25 calls.
Volume was estimated at 80,000 contracts. That figure was above Thursday's final volume of 63,836, according to CBOT figures.
